sections.h2: Which Appling County offices deal with a tax bill?
sections.html:
Two neighboring suites in the Courthouse Annex on Tippins Street in Baxley divide the job. Suite 101 is the Board of Tax Assessors, which decides what your land and house are worth. Suite 102 is the Tax Commissioner, which mails the bill and takes your money.

Calling the wrong door wastes a day, so match the question to the office. Anything about a value, a mistake in the property record, an exemption or an appeal belongs with the assessors. Anything about the amount owed, a payment method or an old balance belongs with the tax commissioner. Property records can be searched at qpublic.net/ga/appling, and the tax commissioner's page points to an online payment portal.

sections.h2: Where does Appling County sit, and who lives in it?
sections.html:
Appling County covers about 507 square miles of land in southeast Georgia, and Baxley, the county seat, is also the largest town. Graham and Surrency are the two other incorporated places, and Holmesville is the old courthouse community that lost the seat to Baxley after an 1872 vote tied to the Macon and Brunswick Railroad.

Census estimates put the county at 19,100 people in July 2025, a gain of 3.5 percent since the 2020 base. That is about 36 residents per square mile. Nearly three in four households own their homes, at 72.5 percent, and the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $76,700 in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Median household income is $46,651. The county issued only 21 building permits in 2025, a small number for a county of this size.

  • The northern third of the county drains to the Altamaha River, and the southern two-thirds drains toward the Little Satilla.
  • The Edwin I. Hatch nuclear plant on U.S. 1 north of Baxley is the area's largest employer.
  • Appling County School District has four elementary schools, a middle school and a high school.
  • Neighbors are Toombs, Tattnall, Wayne, Pierce, Jeff Davis and Bacon counties.

The county and the cities of Baxley, Graham and Surrency prepare a joint comprehensive plan, which is worth a glance if you own land on the edge of town.

sections.h2: How is an Appling County house valued each year?
sections.html:
Assessors fix a value as of January 1, then tax 40 percent of it. The Georgia revenue department spells out the bill this way: assessed value, minus any exemption, times the millage rate, with each mill worth $1 per $1,000 of assessed value.

Appling's assessor page explains the return rules. A return is due January 1 through April 1, but you only need a fresh one when something changed on the parcel, such as a new building or an added acre. Leave out a required return and the county adds a 10 percent penalty on the value you failed to report, plus interest. Business equipment and other personal property gets a return every year, due April 1.

Notices arrive in May. They list the value and carry an estimated bill using the previous year's rates, but the county tells owners this estimate is not a bill. The commissioners and school board have not yet adopted budgets when the notice goes out, and millage usually gets set around September. The commissioners held their FY 2027 budget hearing on October 1, 2026, and scheduled adoption at their October 8 meeting.

sections.h2: What due date should I expect on an Appling bill?
sections.html:
The state default is December 20 with 60 days from billing to pay, but the date printed on your own bill is the one that counts. Georgia's revenue department says most counties use December 20, and it allows exceptions.

Appling bills go to whoever held title on January 1. A June sale does not change that, so a seller can open the mailbox in the fall to a bill for a house they no longer own. The contract and closing statement decide who ends up paying.

  • Pay in the tax commissioner's suite, by mail, or through the county's online portal.
  • Ask for a written payoff on any open year before the closing date.
  • Mobile home owners apply to the tax commissioner for a location permit within 30 days of setting the home, then renew between January 1 and April 1.

Call (912) 367-8105 for the current bill date and any late charges.

sections.h2: How do I challenge an Appling value?
sections.html:
Put the appeal in writing and get it to Suite 101 inside the 45 days that start on the date of your notice. Appling's assessors state that appeals must arrive by the deadline on the notice, and that no appeal can be filed after the period ends.

The grounds are limited to taxability, value and uniformity. A complaint that the tax rate is too high does not qualify. On the state's PT-311A form you choose a route when you file. The assessors review the appeal first, and if they leave the value alone, the file goes to the Board of Equalization, a panel appointed by the grand jury. You can pick arbitration instead, and a hearing officer is open only to non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000.

If you lose, a notice of appeal to Superior Court must reach the assessors within 30 days of the decision. State law requires you to have paid the tax equal to the last year's amount before the court hears it. The revenue department cannot override a local board on a single parcel.

sections.h2: Can I claim a homestead exemption in Appling County?
sections.html:
Yes, if you own the house and live in it as your legal residence. In Appling the application goes to the Tax Assessors' office, which differs from counties where the tax commissioner takes it.

File during the year the home becomes your primary residence, or by April 1 of the next year. The exemption then renews on its own unless you seek a different kind. Appling has raised its local amounts above the state minimum, and the county tax page lists the standard exemption (S1) and a preferential assessment category. Ask the assessors on (912) 367-8108 for the current dollar amounts.

An exemption does not travel with the house. A buyer who moves in has to file in their own name, so a seller's savings stop at closing, and a buyer should plan on a first-year bill that has no exemption in it. The county commissioners also keep a posting about a school district ad valorem exemption on their meetings page.

sections.h2: What if tax is unpaid when I list an Appling County house?
sections.html:
Pay it from the sale proceeds. The tax stays with the parcel, and a county claim that has been recorded as a lien must be cleared before the buyer receives clean title. The revenue department notes that tax liens are recorded in the clerk's office on the general execution docket.

Georgia assigns each year's bill to the January 1 owner and allows no refund for part of a year. The purchase contract is where seller and buyer split the year, and the closing attorney sends the county its share. Estates add one more step: if the owner has died, the Probate Court on South Main Street handles the estate administration.

  • Collect a payoff statement for every open year from Suite 102.
  • Check the clerk's records for any lien on the parcel.
  • Keep your assessment notice with the closing file.
  • Confirm the settlement statement lists the tax line before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Appling County tax bill online?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax commissioner's office points owners to a county online payment portal, and it also takes payments in person at Suite 102, 69 Tippins Street in Baxley, and by mail. The office phone is (912) 367-8105.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value does Appling County tax?
faqs.a: Forty percent of the January 1 fair market value. Exemptions subtract from that assessed figure, and the millage rate then applies to what remains. One mill is $1 for every $1,000 of assessed value.

faqs.q: Is there any way to appeal after the notice period ends?
faqs.a: No. Appling's assessors say an appeal cannot be filed after the 45 days run out. Use the next year's notice for the next chance, and keep the deadline date in view the day the notice lands in your mailbox.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax in the year a house sells?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is billed, but the sales contract can move the cost to the buyer for the months after closing. The closing attorney typically prorates the year and pays the county, so check that the settlement statement shows it.

faqs.q: Which phone number is for value questions?
faqs.a: Dial the Board of Tax Assessors at (912) 367-8108 for values, records, appeals and exemptions. Dial the Tax Commissioner at (912) 367-8105 for billing and payments.
